verses.text: "And in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to support and strengthen him.

"Now I will tell you the truth: Three more kings will rule in Persia, and then a fourth, who will be far richer than all the others. When he has become powerful through his riches, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
Then a mighty king will appear. He will rule with great power and do whatever he wants.

But at the height of his power, his kingdom will be broken up and divided toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, and it will not have the power he had. His kingdom will be torn apart and given to others.
"The king of the south will become strong, but one of his commanders will become even stronger than he is and will rule his own kingdom with great power.

After some years, they will become allies. The daughter of the king of the south will go to the king of the north to make an agreement. But she will not keep her power, and he and his power will not last. She will be handed over, along with those who brought her, her father, and the one who supported her in those times.
"One from her family line will rise to take his place. He will attack the army of the king of the north and enter his fortress. He will fight against them and win.
He will also carry off their gods to Egypt, along with their metal idols and their valuable things of silver and gold. For some years he will leave the king of the north alone.
Then the king of the north will invade the kingdom of the king of the south, but he will go back to his own country.
His sons will prepare for war and gather a great army. It will sweep forward like a flood and carry the battle as far as the enemy's fortress.
"Then the king of the south will march out in anger and fight against the king of the north. The king of the north will raise a large army, but it will be defeated.
When the army is carried off, the king of the south will be filled with pride and will kill many thousands, but he will not stay victorious.
For the king of the north will raise another army, larger than the first. After several years, he will come back with a huge army and plenty of supplies.
"In those times many will rise against the king of the south. Violent men from your own people will rebel to fulfill the vision, but they will fail.
Then the king of the north will come, build siege ramps, and capture a fortified city. The forces of the south will not be able to resist. Even their best troops will not have the strength to stand.
The invader will do as he pleases, and no one will be able to stand against him. He will settle in the beautiful land of Israel and have the power to destroy it.

He will decide to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and he will make an agreement with the king of the south. He will give him a daughter in marriage in order to destroy the kingdom, but his plans will not succeed or help him.
Then he will turn to the coastlands and capture many of them. But a commander will put an end to his insolence and turn his insolence back on him.
After this he will turn back toward the fortresses of his own country, but he will stumble and fall and be seen no more.
"Then someone will take his place who will send out a tax collector to keep up the royal splendor. But in a few days he will be destroyed, though not in anger or in battle.
"He will be replaced by a despised person who has not been given the honor of being king. He will invade the kingdom when its people feel secure, and he will seize it by trickery.
Then great armies will be swept away before him and destroyed, and so will a prince of the covenant.
After making an agreement with him, he will act with deceit. With only a few people he will rise to power.

When the richest provinces feel secure, he will invade them and do what neither his fathers nor his ancestors did. He will hand out plunder, loot, and wealth among his followers. He will plan to overthrow fortresses, but only for a time.

"He will stir up his strength and courage against the king of the south with a large army. The king of the south will go to war with a very large and powerful army, but he will not be able to stand because of the plots against him.
Those who eat from the king's own table will try to destroy him. His army will be swept away, and many will be killed in battle.
The two kings, with their hearts set on evil, will sit at the same table and lie to each other, but it will be of no use, because the end will still come at the appointed time.
The king of the north will return to his own country with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant. He will take action against it and then return to his own country.
"At the appointed time he will invade the south again, but this time the outcome will be different from before.

Ships from the western coastlands will oppose him, and he will lose heart. Then he will turn back and pour out his fury against the holy covenant. He will return and show favor to those who abandon the holy covenant.
"His armed forces will rise up to make the temple fortress unholy and will stop the daily sacrifice. Then they will set up the disgusting thing that causes ruin.
With flattery he will lead astray those who have broken the covenant, but the people who know their God will stand firm and take action.
"Those who are wise will teach many. But for a time they will be killed by the sword or burned, or captured and robbed.
When they fall, they will receive a little help, and many who are not sincere will join them.
Some of the wise will fall, so that they may be refined, purified, and made spotless until the time of the end, because it will still come at the appointed time.

"The king will do as he pleases. He will raise himself up and claim to be greater than every god. He will say unheard-of things against the God of gods. He will be successful until the time of anger is over, because what has been decided must happen.
He will show no respect for the gods of his ancestors, or for the god women love, or for any god at all, because he will claim to be greater than them all.
Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses, a god his ancestors did not know. He will honor it with gold and silver, precious stones, and costly gifts.
He will attack the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god. He will give great honor to those who accept him. He will make them rulers over many people and give them land as a reward.

"At the time of the end, the king of the south will attack him, and the king of the north will storm out against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will invade many countries and sweep through them like a flood.
He will also invade the beautiful land of Israel, and many countries will fall. But Edom, Moab, and the leaders of Ammon will escape his power.
He will reach out his power against many countries, and Egypt will not escape.
He will take control of the treasures of gold and silver and all the riches of Egypt. The Libyans and Cushites will follow at his heels.
But reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will set out in a great rage to destroy and wipe out many.
He will pitch his royal tents between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.
